issues.title: Exact nonlinear source expansion
issues.failure_explanation: The old display claims an exact identity for the general source F. The old source establishes only that q_n and the displayed finite expansion use the degree-N basis; it imposes no condition placing F(q_n(τ),t(τ)) in that span. The admissible N=1 example F(u,t)=t^2 gives τ^2, so the supported object is a degree-one interpolation or projection rather than the exact source function. That exact-versus-approximate distinction is the material mismatch.
issues.overall_effect: The formulation misstates the nonlinear source interpolation as an exact representation. The subsequent nodal construction already has the interpretation of an interpolation, so no formal result depends on exact polynomial closure.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the right-hand polynomial explicitly as the degree-N Lagrange interpolant of F(q_n(·),t(·)) at the quadrature nodes, and replace the asserted exact source identity by an interpolation identity or approximation statement. Make clear that the general source composition itself need not lie in the degree-N span; the existing nodal predictor construction requires no further change.
issues.why_classification: The equality is a well-formed but false exact-closure claim for the advertised general source class, so replacing it by interpolation relinquishes literal exactness and is not merely transcriptional. The replacement is nevertheless recognizably comparable, entirely local, and leaves the method and all formal guarantees unchanged, making the loss limited rather than major.

issues.title: False ADER parameter identity
issues.failure_explanation: For the displayed N=1 nodes, the basis definition gives ψ=((1+√3)/2,(1-√3)/2)^T. Using the displayed first row of a gives (aψ)_0=(4√3-5)/6, which is not w_0=1/2. Algebraically, a=κ^{-1}μ only gives aψ=κ^{-1}diag(w)ψ; the proof supplies no valid reduction to w.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma is false as stated, but the bad identity is not needed downstream. The local-predictor formula uses the separately valid relation κ^{-1}ψ=1, and the endpoint formula uses the valid column identity involving the right-endpoint vector.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false unweighted identity aψ=w by the valid weighted relation a μ^{-1}ψ=1, equivalently Σ_q a_pq ψ_q/w_q=1, and remove the proof steps that infer aψ=w from κ^{-1}ψ=1. Retain the independently valid row-sum, inverse, and right-endpoint identities; no downstream argument needs alteration.
issues.why_classification: The proof makes an invalid algebraic inference, so this is not a typo. The claimed unweighted identity cannot be retained under the stated definitions. A local weighted replacement leaves a recognizable parameter-identity lemma and the rest of the paper intact, but it withdraws one substantive relation, which is a limited weakening appropriate to a moderate issue.

issues.title: Reversed domain-size factor
issues.failure_explanation: For fixed Ω, integrating the uniform bound gives ||u_L-u||_∞^q|Ω|. Hence ||u_L-u||_q≤|Ω|^{1/q}||u_L-u||_∞. The old reciprocal factor does not follow and is false in general, although correcting it leaves the claimed Δt order unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Only the constant in the proof is malformed. The L_q approximation order N+1 and its assumptions remain unchanged after correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the reciprocal domain factor by the multiplicative factor, giving ||u_L-u||_q ≤ [|Ω|·||u_L-u||_∞^q]^(1/q)=|Ω|^(1/q)||u_L-u||_∞, and set C_q=C|Ω|^(1/q).
issues.why_classification: The immediately preceding integral estimate already contains multiplication by |Ω|, so taking the q-th root uniquely forces this correction. No inference, hypothesis, approximation order, or other guarantee changes; the reciprocal is a transcriptional reversal of the constant.

issues.title: Padé degree and matching argument

failure_location.quote: The denominator of $R(z)$ is a polynomial $R_{N, N+1}(z)$ of degree $N$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The matrix $a = \kappa^{-1}\cdot\mu$ in the denominator is invertible and $\mathrm{rank}(a) = N+1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The scalar stability function must be written as det(I-z(a-1w^T))/det(I-za). Since a is invertible of size N+1, the denominator has degree N+1; rank(a-1w^T)=N bounds the numerator degree by N. The old proof instead states degrees N and N-1 and then infers a Padé identity merely from those wrong counts. A valid identification additionally uses the previously proved order 2N+1 to obtain matching through O(z^{2N+2}).
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not establish the Padé theorem. Consequently, its two alternative-proof corollaries, the Padé-based L-stability proof, and the L-stability component of the final stability corollary are not established through this chain until the argument is repaired.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Write the stability function as det(I-z(a-1w^T))/det(I-za). Since a is nonsingular of size N+1, the denominator has degree N+1, while the established rank of a-1w^T bounds the numerator degree by N. Combine these bounds with the previously proved order 2N+1, which gives R(z)-exp(z)=O(z^(2N+2)), and invoke uniqueness of the normalized (N,N+1) Padé approximant. This restores the Padé, A-admissibility, L-stability, and final stability conclusions. On this route, retain the residual statement but do not describe it as an independent alternative proof of the order theorem, because that order was used to identify the Padé approximant.
issues.why_classification: The defect is more than an off-by-one transcription: the old proof omits determinants and the essential Taylor-matching argument. A contained but nontrivial determinant, rank, and Padé-uniqueness argument repairs the theorem and stability chain without new global architecture. Only the independence claimed for one alternative proof must be surrendered, so the loss is limited and the issue is moderate.

issues.title: Endpoint local-solution errors lack a trace convention

failure_location.quote: The following $14$ types of global errors $e$:

issues.failure_explanation: The old prose claims that all 14 displayed quantities are global errors, including four based on a single value u_L(t_n). What the old source actually defines is a sum of indicators for closed cells [t_n,t_{n+1}]. Thus two indicators are active at an interior grid node, giving the literal sum q_{n-1}(1)+q_n(0), while no convention selects the left or right DG trace. The four formulas therefore lack support as errors of one endpoint local-solution trace; this is materially different from the ten unambiguous errors retained in the revision.
issues.overall_effect: Four advertised empirical metrics and their figure/table columns have no specified endpoint-trace interpretation. The formal L_q and essential-supremum results are unaffected because changing values on cell boundaries does not alter those norms.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose a disjoint representative and state its endpoint trace convention. For example, take each cell as (t_n,t_{n+1}], set u_L(t_0)=u_0, and hence define u_L(t_n)=q_{n-1}(1)=u_n for n≥1. Evaluate the four endpoint-based local-solution errors with this left trace and state that they coincide with the corresponding nodal errors. The L_q and essential-supremum results require no change.
issues.why_classification: The literal closed-cell assembly is genuinely ambiguous at grid nodes, so a convention must be supplied and the issue is not a typo. The established endpoint identity provides a standard, source-supported left trace that resolves all four metrics by one local definitional change, without changing the method, convergence rates, empirical quantities, or formal norm results.
